# Setup

If you are running this interactively in Positron and editing the source
`.py` files, add these two lines to your console at the start of each
session. They tell Python to automatically reload any changed files before
each command, so you do not need to restart the kernel after edits:

```python

```

These are IPython magic commands — they only work in the interactive
console (or in a cell here), not in plain `.py` scripts.

# Test 1: Dataset Generation

```{python}
#| label: test-dataset-generation

dataset = make_dataset(
    n_days   = 24,                  # total trials; divisible by 2^n_C and 4
    C_causes = [(14, 0.8)],         # list of (hour, true_cs); first = C01
    E_hour   = 22,                  # clock hour E is observed
    LCSF_hours = [],                # hours for lure confound specified fixed causes
    LUSF_hours = [],                # hours for lure uncorrelated specified fixed causes ... added later so not in all calls
    n_LCIF = 0,                     # N of lure confound interim fixed
    n_LCIR = 0,                     # N of lure confound interim random
    n_LCBF = 0,                     # N of lure confound before-C fixed
    n_LCBR = 0,                     # N of lure confound before-C random
    n_LCAR = 0,                     # N of lure confound any-time random
    n_LUIF = 1,                     # N of lure uncorrelated interim fixed
    n_LUIR = 0,                     # N of lure uncorrelated interim random
    n_LUBF = 0,                     # N of lure uncorrelated before-C fixed
    n_LUBR = 0,                     # N of lure uncorrelated before-C random
    n_LUAR = 0,                     # N of lure uncorrelated any-time random
    n_LSIF = 0,                     # N of lure sporadic interim
    n_LSBF = 0,                     # N of lure sporadic before-C
    n_LSAF = 0,                     # N of lure sporadic any-time
    seed   = 42                     # integer random seed for reproducibility
)

summarise_dataset(dataset)

assert "absolute_hour" in dataset["hour"].columns
assert abs(dataset["day"]["C01"].mean() - 0.5) < 0.01
print("\nDataset generation tests passed.")
```

# Test 2: BayesianNoisyOr — Single Dataset

```{python}
#| label: test-bayesian-simple

dataset_simple = make_dataset(
    n_days   = 24,
    C_causes = [(14, 0.9)],
    E_hour   = 22,
    LCSF_hours = [],
    n_LCIF = 0, n_LCIR = 0, n_LCBF = 0, n_LCBR = 0, n_LCAR = 0,
    n_LUIF = 0, n_LUIR = 0, n_LUBF = 0, n_LUBR = 0, n_LUAR = 0,
    n_LSIF = 0, n_LSBF = 0, n_LSAF = 0,
    seed   = 42
)

bayes_results = run_noisyor_model(
    dataset       = dataset_simple,
    draws         = 2000,
    tune          = 1000,
    chains        = 4,
    target_accept = 0.9,
    random_seed   = 42,
    show_plots    = True,
    verbose       = True
)
```

---

# Test 3: TD Model

```{python}
#| label: test-td-simple

td_results = run_td_model(
    dataset    = dataset_simple,
    alpha      = 0.2,   # learning rate (0, 1]
    beta       = 0.8,   # trace decay (0, 1); higher = longer eligibility memory
    gamma      = 1.0,   # discount factor (0, 1]; 1.0 = no discounting
    show_plots = True,
    verbose    = True
)
```

    n_blocks         = 16,           # N of learning curve checkpoints
    draws            = 1000,        # NUTS posterior samples per chain
    tune             = 500,         # NUTS tuning steps
    chains           = 2,           # N of MCMC chains
    target_accept    = 0.9,         # NUTS target acceptance rate
    random_seed      = 42,          # base random seed
    alpha_avg        = 1.0,         # opacity of average line in learning curve plot
    alpha_individual = 0.5,         # opacity of individual dataset lines
    show_plots       = True,
    verbose          = True
)

# Simulation 1. TD Confounded events before C and interim C-E.

```{python}
ds_no_confound = make_dataset(n_days=48*10, C_causes=[(18, 1.0)], E_hour=22, LCSF_hours=[],      seed=42)
ds_confound_21 = make_dataset(n_days=48*10, C_causes=[(18, 1.0)], E_hour=22, LCSF_hours=[21],    seed=42)
ds_confound_20 = make_dataset(n_days=48*10, C_causes=[(18, 1.0)], E_hour=22, LCSF_hours=[20],    seed=42)
ds_confound_19 = make_dataset(n_days=48*10, C_causes=[(18, 1.0)], E_hour=22, LCSF_hours=[19],    seed=42)
ds_confound_17 = make_dataset(n_days=48*10, C_causes=[(18, 1.0)], E_hour=22, LCSF_hours=[17],    seed=42)
ds_confound_16 = make_dataset(n_days=48*10, C_causes=[(18, 1.0)], E_hour=22, LCSF_hours=[16],    seed=42)
ds_confound_15 = make_dataset(n_days=48*10, C_causes=[(18, 1.0)], E_hour=22, LCSF_hours=[15],    seed=42)

td_no_confound = run_td_model(dataset=ds_no_confound, alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, gamma=1.0, show_plots=False, verbose=False)
td_confound_21 = run_td_model(dataset=ds_confound_21, alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, gamma=1.0, show_plots=False, verbose=False)
td_confound_20 = run_td_model(dataset=ds_confound_20, alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, gamma=1.0, show_plots=False, verbose=False)
td_confound_19 = run_td_model(dataset=ds_confound_19, alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, gamma=1.0, show_plots=False, verbose=False)
td_confound_17 = run_td_model(dataset=ds_confound_17, alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, gamma=1.0, show_plots=False, verbose=False)
td_confound_16 = run_td_model(dataset=ds_confound_16, alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, gamma=1.0, show_plots=False, verbose=False)
td_confound_15 = run_td_model(dataset=ds_confound_15, alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, gamma=1.0, show_plots=False, verbose=False)



# Extract final weights for C01 and the confound in each condition
# No confound has no confound weight to extract

conditions = {
    "No confound"   : (td_no_confound, None),
    "Confound hr 21": (td_confound_21, "LCSF01_21"),
    "Confound hr 20": (td_confound_20, "LCSF01_20"),
    "Confound hr 19": (td_confound_19, "LCSF01_19"),
    "Confound hr 17": (td_confound_17, "LCSF01_17"),
    "Confound hr 16": (td_confound_16, "LCSF01_16"),
    "Confound hr 15": (td_confound_15, "LCSF01_15"),
}

print(f"{'Condition':<18} {'w_C01':>8} {'w_confound':>10}")
print(f"{'-'*18} {'-'*8} {'-'*10}")

c01_weights      = []
confound_weights = []
labels_plot      = []

for label, (td_result, confound_name) in conditions.items():
    cause_cols = td_result["cause_cols"]
    w_final    = td_result["w_final"]
    
    c01_w      = w_final[cause_cols.index("C01")]
    confound_w = w_final[cause_cols.index(confound_name)] if confound_name in cause_cols else float("nan")
    
    print(f"{label:<18} {c01_w:>8.4f} {confound_w:>10.4f}")
    c01_weights.append(c01_w)
    confound_weights.append(confound_w)
    labels_plot.append(label)




fig2, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))

x     = np.arange(len(labels_plot))
width = 0.6

no_confound_val = c01_weights[0]

# Left panel — C01
ax1.bar(x, c01_weights, width, color="#1565C0", alpha=0.8)
ax1.axhline(y=no_confound_val, color="black", linewidth=1.5, linestyle="--",
            label=f"No confound = {no_confound_val:.8f}")
ax1.set_xticks(x)
ax1.set_xticklabels(labels_plot, rotation=15, ha="right", fontsize=9)
ax1.set_ylabel("Final associative weight")
ax1.set_title("C01 weight by confound position")
ymin1 = min(c01_weights) * 0.95
ymax1 = max(c01_weights) * 1.05
ax1.set_ylim(ymin1, ymax1)
ax1.legend(fontsize=8)

# Right panel — Confound only (skip no confound condition)
confound_labels = [l for l, v in zip(labels_plot, confound_weights) if not np.isnan(v)]
confound_vals   = [v for v       in confound_weights                if not np.isnan(v)]
x2 = np.arange(len(confound_labels))

ax2.bar(x2, confound_vals, width, color="#E65100", alpha=0.8)
ax2.set_xticks(x2)
ax2.set_xticklabels(confound_labels, rotation=15, ha="right", fontsize=9)
ax2.set_ylabel("Final associative weight")
ax2.set_title("Confound weight by confound position")
ymin2 = min(confound_vals) * 0.95
ymax2 = max(confound_vals) * 1.05
ax2.set_ylim(ymin2, ymax2)

fig2.suptitle("TD Final Weights: C01 vs Confound by Confound Position\n"
              "(C01 at hr 18, E at hr 22, beta=0.95, 10 steps/hr)",
              fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
fig2.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.95])
plt.show()

```

# Simulation 4. Adding 1000 timesteps per hour for TD
```{python}
dataset_hourly = make_dataset(
    n_days     = 24,
    C_causes   = [(16, 1.0)],
    E_hour     = 22,
    LUSF_hours = [],
    n_LCIF = 0, n_LCIR = 0, n_LCBF = 0, n_LCBR = 0, n_LCAR = 0,
    n_LUIF = 0, n_LUIR = 0, n_LUBF = 0, n_LUBR = 0, n_LUAR = 0,
    n_LSIF = 0, n_LSBF = 0, n_LSAF = 0,
    seed   = 42
)

dataset_hourly_expanded = expand_to_substeps(
    dataset        = dataset_hourly,
    steps_per_hour = 1000
)

td_hourly = run_td_model(
    dataset    = dataset_hourly,
    alpha      = 0.2,
    beta       = 0.8,
    gamma      = 1.0,
    show_plots = False,
    verbose    = False
)

td_hourly_expanded = run_td_model(
    dataset    = dataset_hourly_expanded,
    alpha      = 0.2,
    beta       = 0.8,
    gamma      = 1.0,
    show_plots = False,
    verbose    = False
)

print(f"Final w_C01 (hourly)          : {td_hourly['w_final'][0]:.4f}")
print(f"Final w_C01 (hourly expanded) : {td_hourly_expanded['w_final'][0]:.4f}")

def plot_td_timescale_comparison(td_results_list, labels, steps_per_hour_list,
                                  show=True):
    """
    Compare TD weight trajectories across different timescale resolutions.

    Converts the x-axis to days so that hourly and minute-level results
    are directly comparable on the same scale.

    Parameters
    ----------
    td_results_list    : list of run_td_model() output dicts
    labels             : list of str, one label per result
    steps_per_hour_list: list of int, steps_per_hour used for each dataset.
                         Use 1 for the original hourly dataset.
    show               : bool, call plt.show() (default True)
    """
    import matplotlib.cm as cm
    tab10       = cm.get_cmap("tab10")
    cond_colors = [tab10(i % 10) for i in range(len(td_results_list))]

    # Get cause names from first result
    cause_cols = td_results_list[0]["cause_cols"]
    n_causes   = len(cause_cols)

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        nrows   = n_causes,
        ncols   = 1,
        figsize = (10, 3.5 * n_causes),
        squeeze = False
    )

    for ci, cause in enumerate(cause_cols):
        ax = axes[ci, 0]

        for res, label, color, steps in zip(
            td_results_list, labels, cond_colors, steps_per_hour_list
        ):
            w_history  = res["w_history"][:, ci]   # weights for this cause
            n_steps    = len(w_history)
            steps_per_day = 24 * steps

            # Convert timestep index to days
            days = np.arange(n_steps) / steps_per_day

            ax.plot(days, w_history, color=color, linewidth=1.5, label=label)

        ax.set_title(cause, fontsize=9, fontweight="bold")
        ax.set_xlabel("Day", fontsize=8)
        ax.set_ylabel("Associative weight (w)", fontsize=8)
        ax.legend(fontsize=7)

        # Free y-axis
        all_vals = np.concatenate([r["w_history"][:, ci] for r in td_results_list])
        ymin, ymax = np.nanmin(all_vals), np.nanmax(all_vals)
        pad = max((ymax - ymin) * 0.1, 0.02)
        ax.set_ylim(ymin - pad, ymax + pad)

    fig.suptitle("TD Weight Trajectories — Timescale Comparison",
                 fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.97])
    if show:
        plt.show()
    return fig


fig = plot_td_timescale_comparison(
    td_results_list     = [td_hourly, td_hourly_expanded],
    labels              = ["Hourly", "Hourly Expanded (1000 steps/hr)"],
    steps_per_hour_list = [1, 1000],
    show                = True
)

```

TD basically learns nothing
Final w_C01 (hourly)          : 0.1272
Final w_C01 (hourly expanded) : 0.0000







# Simulation 5. TD Modifying β (Beta) – the trace decay/persistence rate
Near 0: the eligibility trace vanishes almost immediately after a stimulus fires, so only causes that occurred in the very last timestep can receive credit. Effectively no memory of past stimuli.
Near 1: the trace decays very slowly, so causes that fired many timesteps ago still have a strong trace and can receive substantial credit. Long temporal memory.
```{python}
dataset_hourly = make_dataset(
    n_days     = 24,
    C_causes   = [(16, 1.0)],
    E_hour     = 22,
    LUSF_hours = [],
    n_LCIF = 0, n_LCIR = 0, n_LCBF = 0, n_LCBR = 0, n_LCAR = 0,
    n_LUIF = 0, n_LUIR = 0, n_LUBF = 0, n_LUBR = 0, n_LUAR = 0,
    n_LSIF = 0, n_LSBF = 0, n_LSAF = 0,
    seed   = 42
)

td_hourly_beta80 = run_td_model(
    dataset    = dataset_hourly,
    alpha      = 0.2,        # learning rate (0, 1]
    beta       = 0.8,        # trace decay (0, 1)
    gamma      = 1.0,        # discount factor (0, 1]
    show_plots = False,
    verbose    = False
)

td_hourly_beta30 = run_td_model(
    dataset    = dataset_hourly,
    alpha      = 0.2,        # learning rate (0, 1]
    beta       = 0.3,        # trace decay (0, 1)
    gamma      = 1.0,        # discount factor (0, 1]
    show_plots = False,
    verbose    = False
)

print(f"Final w_C01 (beta = 0.8) : {td_hourly_beta80['w_final'][0]:.4f}")
print(f"Final w_C01 (beta = 0.3) : {td_hourly_beta30['w_final'][0]:.4f}")

fig = plot_td_timescale_comparison(
    td_results_list     = [td_hourly_beta80, td_hourly_beta30],
    labels              = ["beta = 0.8", "beta = 0.3"],
    steps_per_hour_list = [1, 1],
    show                = True
)


```

Final w_C01 (beta = 0.8) : 0.1272
Final w_C01 (beta = 0.3) : 0.0020







# Simulation 6. TD Modifying Ɣ (Gamma)
Near 0: future predictions are worth almost nothing. The model only cares about immediate reward, making it very myopic.
At 1.0: no discounting at all — a prediction of reward 1000 timesteps in the future is worth exactly the same as an immediate reward. 
```{python}
dataset_hourly = make_dataset(
    n_days     = 24*1000,
    C_causes   = [(16, 1.0)],
    E_hour     = 22,
    LUSF_hours = [],
    n_LCIF = 0, n_LCIR = 0, n_LCBF = 0, n_LCBR = 0, n_LCAR = 0,
    n_LUIF = 0, n_LUIR = 0, n_LUBF = 0, n_LUBR = 0, n_LUAR = 0,
    n_LSIF = 0, n_LSBF = 0, n_LSAF = 0,
    seed   = 42
)

td_hourly_gamma10 = run_td_model(
    dataset    = dataset_hourly,
    alpha      = 0.9,        # learning rate (0, 1]
    beta       = 0.8,        # trace decay (0, 1)
    gamma      = 1.0,        # discount factor (0, 1]
    show_plots = False,
    verbose    = False
)

td_hourly_gamma05 = run_td_model(
    dataset    = dataset_hourly,
    alpha      = 0.9,        # learning rate (0, 1]
    beta       = 0.8,        # trace decay (0, 1)
    gamma      = 0.1,        # discount factor (0, 1]
    show_plots = False,
    verbose    = False
)

print(f"Final w_C01 (gamma = 1.0) : {td_hourly_gamma10['w_final'][0]:.4f}")
print(f"Final w_C01 (gamma = 0.5) : {td_hourly_gamma05['w_final'][0]:.4f}")

fig = plot_td_timescale_comparison(
    td_results_list     = [td_hourly_gamma10, td_hourly_gamma05],
    labels              = ["gamma = 1.0", "gamma = 0.5"],
    steps_per_hour_list = [1, 1],
    show                = True
)


```


# More for Understanding Gamma. Not reported in paper.

short vs. medium vs. long delay when gamma = 0 vs. 1
There is basically no learning in the long delay, 
Those little peaks or dips in the long delay (if you zoom in) arise in TD so long as E doesn't come right after C. I added medium delay to also show the tiny dips.
The key thing is that changing Gamma from 0 to 1 has essentially no impact in this paradigm, for short medium or long delay.
